original_question: If Δ is the maximum vertex degree of a nontrivial graph G, does there always exist a signature σ such that the spectral radius of the resulting signed graph satisfies ρ(G, σ) < 2 sqrt(Δ - 1)?
target_in_paper: Section 3.5, Conjecture 3.25 ([46]), presented as Gregory's variant of the Bilu-Linial conjecture after dropping the regularity assumption.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official target very closely. It has the right parameter (the maximum/largest vertex degree Δ), the right class of objects (a nontrivial graph G together with a signature σ), the right spectral quantity (the spectral radius of the signed graph), and the exact strict bound ρ(G,σ) < 2√(Δ-1). Those are precisely the core ingredients of Conjecture 3.25.
missing_details: State explicitly that G is the underlying unsigned graph and that a signature is a map σ:E(G)→{+1,-1}.
Define ρ(G,σ) as the spectral radius of the signed adjacency matrix Aσ, i.e. the maximum absolute value of its eigenvalues.
For a fully stand-alone formulation, note that Aσ is a real symmetric {0,+1,-1}-matrix attached to the signed graph (G,σ).
The paper's official statement uses only 'nontrivial graph G'; it does not add a connectedness hypothesis here, so connectedness should not be inserted.
Contextually, this is posed as a nonregular variant of Conjecture 3.20 in Section 3.5; it should not be replaced by the stronger spectral-radius question in Problem 3.26.
refined_question: Let G be a nontrivial finite graph with largest vertex degree Δ, and let σ:E(G)→{+1,-1} be a signature on its edges. If Aσ denotes the signed adjacency matrix of the signed graph (G,σ), does there always exist such a signature σ for which the spectral radius ρ(Aσ)=ρ(G,σ) satisfies ρ(G,σ) < 2√(Δ-1)?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Section 3.5, Conjecture 3.25 (p. 12), whose statement matches your draft essentially verbatim: if Δ is the largest vertex degree of a nontrivial graph G, then there exists a signature σ such that ρ(G,σ) < 2√(Δ-1). The surrounding discussion confirms that this is the correct target and not a neighboring problem. Problem 3.18 (p. 10) is the broader optimization problem of finding signatures minimizing spectral radius; Conjecture 3.20 (p. 10) is the d-regular Bilu-Linial version; Theorem 3.21 (pp. 10-11) is the Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava partial result controlling only the largest eigenvalue; and Problem 3.26 (p. 12) is a stronger question involving the ordinary spectral radius ρ(G), which the paper explicitly says would imply Conjecture 3.25 rather than be equivalent to it. The notation needed to make the question stand-alone comes from the Introduction (pp. 1-2), where a signed graph Γ=(G,σ), its signed adjacency matrix, and its spectral radius are defined, and from Section 3.5 (p. 10), which identifies the spectral radius of a signing with the spectral radius of Aσ.
